title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. 𝔛 is a variety (the margin note says 𝔛 = X̄, the base change to Q̄ of some X) of finite type over Q̄. Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q). The other groups are:
- G_𝔛 is the group of Galois-semilinear automorphisms of 𝔛, i.e. pairs (σ, u) with σ ∈ Γ and u: 𝔛 → 𝔛 an isomorphism lying over σ. It maps to Γ.
- E_𝔛 is the analogous group for the universal cover 𝔛̃.
- These fit in the exact sequence (6): 1 → π1(𝔛) → E_𝔛 → G_𝔛 → 1, with π1(𝔛) = Aut(𝔛̃/𝔛).
- For a point ξ ∈ 𝔛(Q̄), G_𝔛(ξ) is the stabilizer of ξ. Choosing 𝔛̃ = 𝔛̃(ξ), the universal cover pointed over ξ, gives a partial splitting G_𝔛(ξ) → E_𝔛 (8).

This page, step ③. Because 𝔛 is of finite type over Q̄, it descends to a number field K. This gives a 'germ of lifting' (9): a homomorphism Γ' → G_𝔛 defined on some open subgroup Γ' ⊂ Γ and lifting the inclusion Γ' ⊂ Γ. It is well defined only up to the equivalence 'agree on a smaller open subgroup'; descent data for different models differ by such germs.

Fix ξ. For Γ' small enough, meaning Γ' fixes ξ (ξ is defined over the corresponding field K'), the map Γ' → G_𝔛 lands in the stabilizer G_𝔛(ξ). Composing with the splitting (8) gives a germ of homomorphism φ_ξ: Γ' → E_𝔛 compatible with the projections, as in diagram (10). If 𝔛̃ is not the cover pointed at ξ, φ_ξ is only defined up to conjugation by elements of π1(𝔛). The next page stresses that only the germ of φ_ξ is defined, i.e. up to restriction to finite-index subgroups.

In modern terms, φ_ξ is the Galois section s_ξ: Gal(Q̄/K') → π1(X_{K'}) attached to a rational point, defined up to π1-conjugacy. The new twist is that it is taken as a germ over the open subgroups of Γ. This gives a map
 X(Q̄) → lim_{K'} {sections of π1(X_{K'}) → G_{K'}}/conjugacy,
formulated intrinsically for a variety over Q̄ via the semilinear automorphism group. This is the setting of the section conjecture.

The crossed-out block at the top concerns proving injectivity of points → sections. One embeds 𝔛 injectively into a commutative algebraic group of unipotent rank 0 (a semi-abelian variety: an abelian variety extended by a torus, e.g. the generalized Jacobian/Albanese of an open curve) via 𝔛(Q̄) → J. One then uses the Kummer map. This continues on the next page, (11): η_ξ ∈ lim Hom(Γ', Ext(π1, …)) and its image in an H^1.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The statement that Γ' → G_𝔛 factors through G_𝔛(ξ) for Γ' small enough uses that the lift Γ' → G_𝔛 comes from a K'-model in which ξ is K'-rational. This is implicit but correct.

Injectivity via a semi-abelian variety needs 𝔛 to inject into it (e.g. genus ≥ 1, or a hyperbolic open curve via its generalized Jacobian). It also needs injectivity of the Kummer map on a finitely generated Mordell–Weil group over number fields. The step is only sketched and was crossed out.

ideas.what: Section of the arithmetic fundamental group attached to a rational point, defined up to π1-conjugacy, via the pointed universal cover and the stabilizer of ξ
ideas.modern_name: Section s_ξ associated to a rational point (section conjecture setup)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings, 1983; Esquisse d'un programme 1984)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983); Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Formulation for a variety over Q̄ using the group of Galois-semilinear automorphisms and 'germs' of liftings Γ' → G_𝔛 over open subgroups, modulo restriction
ideas.modern_name: Limit over finite extensions of section sets / 'section conjecture over K̄' (pro-version, X(K̄) → lim_L S_{π1(X_L/L)})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in later literature (e.g. Stix's monograph discusses limits of sections over finite extensions)

ideas.what: Injectivity of points → sections via embedding into a semi-abelian variety (extension of an abelian variety by a torus) and the Kummer map
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the section conjecture via the (generalized) Albanese/Jacobian and Kummer theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; written up e.g. by Stix, Nakamura, Mochizuki

missed.claim: Dated evidence (c. 1980–81, before the 1983 Faltings letter) that Grothendieck had already set up the map from rational points to (germs of) Galois sections, together with the semi-abelian/Kummer approach to its injectivity. He did so intrinsically for varieties over Q̄ via the semilinear automorphism group G_𝔛 and germs over open subgroups of Gal(Q̄/Q).
missed.quote: Pour ξ ∈ 𝔛(Q̄) donné, et pour Γ' assez petit, Γ' → G_𝔛 se factorise par G_𝔛(ξ), d'où sort un germe d'homom. compatible Γ' → E_𝔛
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This matters historically, as a pre-1983 genesis of the section conjecture. The 'germ' formulation is also a natural intrinsic framework for the section conjecture over Q̄ (independent of a chosen model) that is rarely stated this way.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard point-to-section construction, close to what appears in the 1983 Faltings letter. What is mildly notable is the early date and the model-independent 'germ' formalism via Galois-semilinear automorphisms of 𝔛/Q̄. No new theorem appears.
transcription_corrections: In (9) and the following lines, 'G_{x̄}' should read G_𝔛 (script X), the group of semilinear automorphisms. The bar is part of the handwriting/notation, not a point x̄.
'd'où sort [?] {+germe d'+} un homom.' should read 'd'où sort un germe d'homom. compatible Γ' → E_𝔛'.

'– de même si X̃ = 𝔛(ξ) – on obtient un homom défini mod composition par un auto-morph. [?]' is probably '— du moins si 𝔛̃ = 𝔛̃(ξ) — sinon on obtient un homom défini mod composition par un automorph. intérieur provenant de π1(𝔛)'. This matches the parallel sentence on the previous page.
The arrow in (10) is labelled φ_ξ (from Γ' to E_𝔛).
In the margin, '𝔛 = X̄' indicates that 𝔛 is the base change to Q̄ of a variety X.
